parameters.name: V33_ROUTE_MODEL_TEASTORE
parameters.unit: TeaStore pause regimes with their explicit target services, the one regime P1 and P2 are declared for, the declared affected path of the off-path target
parameters.origin_ref: research/PLAN_LANES_20261014.md S2 ('reader: second pause regime trips pause_regime() assert'). v2.4's pause_regime() asserts exactly one stopping regime per system (sweep_analysis_v2.py:2836-2839); with the off-path epoch TeaStore has two (recommender pause, auth freeze). The reader accepts exactly this pair with these targets and refuses any other set of stopping regimes or any other target for either (UnknownSchema), and P1 and P2 stay declared for the request-path pause (auth-freeze), as v3.2 did for OTel (V32_ROUTE_MODEL_OTEL.p1p2Regime). The off-path target's affected path is the target alone (the project map's route graph is restricted to webui/auth/persistence/image, so v1.path_of already returns {target} for a service off the route); the registry service is deliberately NOT added to it: that would change which registry spikes count (a rule), and this version is admission and reporting only. The coordinator may decide otherwise before the freeze. syncServices, edges and asyncEdges are empty because no TeaStore call graph is declared here (the project map's is used, as for every TeaStore epoch). Re-pinned 2026-10-14: the pause regimes and their targets are those of teastore-offpath-v1.json at f74b29b (faultParameters, candidate_offpath_ts.FAULT_TARGETS) and DECLARATION_TEASTORE_OFFPATH.md (f40e786); the registry service stays off the recommender's declared path, as in the draft (not a rule change); the lanes block reports its fires.

parameters.unit: per system: the rule that assigns a counted fire to a lane (own / coordinator / lag) by service name, channel and metric-name family
parameters.origin_ref: research/PLAN_LANES_20261014.md directions S1 and S2 and the lane table (lane 1 own silence, lane 2 coordinator side, lane 3 backlog/lag); lead's brief of 2026-10-14. Ids are matched by RULE (service name, channel, metric-name prefix), never by hard-coded hash: a log id is a template hash and changes with the log text. `coordinator` is therefore every log id of the service, a SUPERSET of the Kafka group-coordinator lines (a rule by service, not by message text: frozen regexes were a major prior failure, memory no-narrow-regex-heuristics). `kafka` and `registry` are the service names the catalog and the TeaStore log layout give; `kafka` is in research/otel-offpath/adapter.py APP_SERVICES, so a resource with service.name=kafka is admitted without an adapter edit (BUDGET_F.md change 3 upserts that name on the kafkametrics resources; a resource WITHOUT service.name is dropped by the adapter, `nonServiceResources`). Own fires are reported in `own` only; a fire is in at most one lane (own first, then coordinator, then lag). Only COUNTED fires enter the counted field of a lane: `counts` (the spike path filter) and no BC flag, which is celf_v3's `counted` for a sensor under decision 72 (a by-construction fire is a miss); a fire with `counts` True and a non-empty BC flag list is reported beside it as `earliestByConstruction` with its flags, labelled 'by construction, not counted' (added 2026-10-14 on the coordinator's request: the TeaStore registry heartbeat-removal log id fires in every auth-freeze episode but is BC-caller-log flagged, so a counted-only row would read miss by rule). TeaStore has no consumer-group lag lane (`null`): its lag cell reads `—`. The lanes are a report only; they change no calibration, rule, placement or score. Re-pinned 2026-10-14: the OTel `kafka` service name is the harness's kafkametrics resourceServiceName (candidate_offpath_f.KAFKAMETRICS, 715d57b); the TeaStore `registry` is the compose service whose lines application.log keeps (candidate_offpath_ts.py collection.registryLog, f74b29b); lane predictions are in the two declarations (F-L1/L2/L3/M, T-L1/T-L2/T-OFF/T-C).

parameters.name: V33_LANES_REPORT_RULE
parameters.value: Per regime (and per rate), for every fault episode, the earliest COUNTED fire of each lane: (a) own = sensors of the episode's target (excluded from the placement by decisions 84/111; this is a separate report row, the exclusion is unchanged), (b) coordinator = log ids of the system's coordinator service, (c) lag = consumer-group lag metric ids. A lane's cell reads `—` (JSON null) when no sensor of the lane was collected in the cell (`collectedSensors` 0) and 0 fires when sensors were collected and none fired; the summary counts episodes with a fire over episodes with collected sensors, never over all episodes. Beside the counted fire, each lane carries the earliest fire dropped ONLY by a BC flag (`earliestByConstruction`, with `bcFlags`, label 'by construction, not counted'); counting, placement and the pass rule are unchanged. The time is the fire's `ttd` in seconds after the onset command, the readout's conservative time (a whole-second log stamp is timed at the end of its second, detection_time.log_ttd); `ttdLo` is the lower end. Scope: instance (one SUT, one host, one campaign); nothing is a mechanism claim.
